summary: H.R. 1702, known as the JUDGES Act of 2025, addresses judicial understaffing by creating 64 new U.S. district court judgeships across multiple states over a ten-year period, establishing 63 permanent positions and 1 temporary position. It also expands court locations in California and Texas, requires GAO reports on judicial workloads and detention space, and mandates online public access to the Judicial Conference's biennial judgeship recommendations.

affected_groups.effect: Receives 64 new judgeships (63 permanent, 1 temporary) to handle pending cases and rising workloads over a 10-year rollout.
affected_groups.group: Federal Judiciary and U.S. District Courts

affected_groups.effect: Gains designated court locations in College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, alongside numerous new judgeships allocated to district courts in both states.
affected_groups.group: Residents and Litigants in Texas and California

affected_groups.effect: Required to conduct and submit evaluations to Congress on judicial workloads, methodologies, senior judge policies, and federal agency detention space.
Required to make the biennial report of judgeship recommendations publicly available on its website and submit copies to congressional committees.
affected_groups.group: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts

key_provisions: Creates 63 new permanent district court judgeships across 14 states phased in between 2025 and 2035.
Creates one temporary district court judgeship in the Eastern District of Oklahoma in 2025.
Expands court location requirements by adding College Station to the Houston Division of the Southern District of Texas and El Centro to the Southern District of California.
Authorizes specific appropriations starting at $12,965,330 for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, scaling up to $61,122,270 for fiscal year 2035 and beyond, with annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

Directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to submit reports to congressional committees evaluating judicial caseloads, workload measures, senior judge policies, and federal detention space needs within two years of enactment.
Requires the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts to publish the biennial report on Article III judgeship recommendations by the Judicial Conference on its website free of charge.
missing_information: The precise criteria or formula used to select the exact number of judgeships for each specific district court beyond referencing the Judicial Conference's 2023 report.
Specific details on how the GAO will execute its assessments on federal agency detention space acquisition challenges.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 1702, known as the JUDGES Act of 2025, addresses judicial understaffing by creating 64 new U.S. district court judgeships across multiple states over a ten-year period, establishing 63 permanent positions and 1 temporary position. It also expands court locations in California and Texas, requires GAO reports on judicial workloads and detention space, and mandates online public access to the Judicial Conference's biennial judgeship recommendations.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a comprehensive expansion of the federal district court judiciary—the first new permanent judgeships authorized since 2003—authorizing dozens of new judicial positions and matching funding phased in over a decade across 14 states, alongside targeted structural and reporting mandates.
